The fragment entries are d1br0a_ (sunid 17772; NMR, 120-residue Habc fragment) and d1ez3a_/b_/c_ (sunids 17768-17770; 1.9 A crystal, 124-residue Habc fragment), both under the curated protein node 'Syntaxin 1A N-terminal domain' (sunid 47663, Norway rat species 47664). The full-domain entry 1dn1 chain B is d1dn1b_ (sunid 302344, 222 residues spanning Habc, linker and the H3 SNARE motif), and its replacement 3c98 chain B is d3c98b_ (sunid 173092, 247 residues including the N-peptide). All are defined as single whole-chain domains.

Three aspects of SCOPe's treatment change the interpretation of fragment-based fold assignments.

1. The fold assignment made from the fragments is confirmed, but only for the Habc core. The three-helix Habc bundle seen in 1br0 and 1ez3 is the same a.47 STAT-like fold found in the full-length closed syntaxin of 3c98 B, so the fragment-derived fold label was correct for that region. This is a family-level (homology) statement among t-SNARE Habc domains (syntaxin 1A, syntaxin 6 d1lvfa_, squid syntaxin d1s94a_), and nothing stronger: the a.47 fold also contains the unrelated a.47.1 superfamily, so fold-level similarity does not imply common ancestry, and the Habc fold itself does not predict Munc18 binding or fusion function.

2. The whole-chain domain definitions for 1dn1 B and 3c98 B absorb about 100 extra residues (linker plus H3) into an a.47.2.1 domain, even though H3 is not part of the STAT-like fold. SCOPe classifies that same syntaxin 1A segment, when it is in the four-helix SNARE complex, in class h (h.1.15.1 'SNARE fusion complex', superfamily 58038, family 58039, protein 'Syntaxin 1A' sunid 88908; e.g. d1n7sb1 1n7s B:191-256, d1sfcb_). Class h is a coiled-coil structural descriptor, not an evolutionary fold. So a fold label derived from a fragment cannot be transferred to the whole chain: the H3 region's structural state is conformation- and partner-dependent (packed against Habc in the closed Munc18-bound form, extended coiled coil in the SNARE complex), and the single SCCS attached to the full chain hides a region whose classification differs by context. The Munc18 partner (chain A) is classified separately in e.25.1.1 and contributes nothing to the syntaxin fold assignment.

3. For the full-length closed syntaxin, 3c98 B (curated, 2.6 A, R-factor 0.208, AEROSPACI 0.31) is the appropriate representative, not the obsolete 1dn1 (AEROSPACI 0.25). For the Habc domain alone, 1ez3 (AEROSPACI 0.47, 1.9 A) is the best template; 1br0 is an NMR fragment with AEROSPACI 0.036 and effective resolution 4 A and should not be used as a template.

Limits: SCOPe gives no residue-range split of 1dn1 B or 3c98 B, so the boundary between the Habc core and the H3/linker region must be taken from the structures themselves and from SNARE-complex entries, not from the SCCS. Homology inference should stop at the a.47.2.1 family; conformational and functional conclusions about H3 require the full-length coordinates (3c98), SNARE complex structures (1sfc, 1n7s) and independent biochemical evidence of the open/closed equilibrium.

Current SCOPe (release 2.08, frozen 2021-07-28, latest periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16) places all of these structures in the same family, a.47.2.1 't-snare proteins' (family sunid 47662, superfamily a.47.2 sunid 47661, fold a.47 'STAT-like' sunid 47654, class a). The fragment entries are d1br0a_ (sunid 17772; NMR, 120-residue Habc fragment) and d1ez3a_/b_/c_ (sunids 17768-17770; 1.9 A crystal, 124-residue Habc fragment), both under the curated protein node 'Syntaxin 1A N-terminal domain' (sunid 47663, Norway rat species 47664). The full-domain entry 1dn1 chain B is d1dn1b_ (sunid 302344, 222 residues spanning Habc, linker and the H3 SNARE motif), and its replacement 3c98 chain B is d3c98b_ (sunid 173092, 247 residues including the N-peptide). All are defined as single whole-chain domains.

Three aspects of SCOPe's treatment change the interpretation of fragment-based fold assignments.

1. The fold assignment made from the fragments is confirmed, but only for the Habc core. The three-helix Habc bundle seen in 1br0 and 1ez3 is the same a.47 STAT-like fold found in the full-length closed syntaxin of 3c98 B, so the fragment-derived fold label was correct for that region. This is a family-level (homology) statement among t-SNARE Habc domains (syntaxin 1A, syntaxin 6 d1lvfa_, squid syntaxin d1s94a_), and nothing stronger: the a.47 fold also contains the unrelated a.47.1 superfamily, so fold-level similarity does not imply common ancestry, and the Habc fold itself does not predict Munc18 binding or fusion function.

2. The whole-chain domain definitions for 1dn1 B and 3c98 B absorb about 100 extra residues (linker plus H3) into an a.47.2.1 domain, even though H3 is not part of the STAT-like fold. SCOPe classifies that same syntaxin 1A segment, when it is in the four-helix SNARE complex, in class h (h.1.15.1 'SNARE fusion complex', superfamily 58038, family 58039, protein 'Syntaxin 1A' sunid 88908; e.g. d1n7sb1 1n7s B:191-256, d1sfcb_). Class h is a coiled-coil structural descriptor, not an evolutionary fold. So a fold label derived from a fragment cannot be transferred to the whole chain: the H3 region's structural state is conformation- and partner-dependent (packed against Habc in the closed Munc18-bound form, extended coiled coil in the SNARE complex), and the single SCCS attached to the full chain hides a region whose classification differs by context. The Munc18 partner (chain A) is classified separately in e.25.1.1 and contributes nothing to the syntaxin fold assignment.

3. Representative selection and template use must respect obsolescence and curation status. 1dn1 was obsoleted on 2008-03-25 and superseded by 3c98 ('Revised structure of the munc18a-syntaxin1 complex'). d1dn1b_ was manually curated in SCOP 1.75 (then sunid 17771 under node 47663), was absent from SCOPe 2.01-2.05, and was re-added in 2.06 as a new sunid (302344) under 'automated matches' (protein node 191190, species node 311131). Its family assignment is therefore inherited by sequence identity to curated domains and is not independent structural evidence; FATCAT chain statistics are not applicable for either d1br0a_ or d1dn1b_, and no AlphaFold structure matches are recorded for d1br0a_. For the full-length closed syntaxin, 3c98 B (curated, 2.6 A, R-factor 0.208, AEROSPACI 0.31) is the appropriate representative, not the obsolete 1dn1 (AEROSPACI 0.25). For the Habc domain alone, 1ez3 (AEROSPACI 0.47, 1.9 A) is the best template; 1br0 is an NMR fragment with AEROSPACI 0.036 and effective resolution 4 A and should not be used as a template.

Limits: SCOPe gives no residue-range split of 1dn1 B or 3c98 B, so the boundary between the Habc core and the H3/linker region must be taken from the structures themselves and from SNARE-complex entries, not from the SCCS. Homology inference should stop at the a.47.2.1 family; conformational and functional conclusions about H3 require the full-length coordinates (3c98), SNARE complex structures (1sfc, 1n7s) and independent biochemical evidence of the open/closed equilibrium.
